newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr stands tall by late Tokyo but topside capped.
newsitem.headline: Dlr stands tall by late Tokyo but topside capped.

text.p: 0639 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar stood tall against the yen and the mark by late Tokyo trade on Monday, carrying over a bullish undertone, but its advance was limited amid a lack of convincing follow-through buying, dealers said.
Activity was led by day-traders who were unwilling to drive the dollar up decisively against the yen due to concerns over possible verbal intervention by Japanese authorities.
The dollar received a temporary boost against the yen in the afternoon in reaction to weakness in the Japanese stock market and falls in the yield of Japanese government bonds.
"The underlying weakness in the Japanese equities market was starting to hurt the trend of the yen," said Yoh Nihei, a manager at Sakura Bank in Tokyo.

But the dollar's rise was shortlived as stocks recovered slightly from their low and JGBs also climbed back after the yield of the 182nd 10-year JGB fell to a record low of 2.070 percent. At 0648 GMT, the key yield stood at 2.110 percent, up 0.005 from Friday's closing level.

JGB yields recovered due to a news agency report quoting comments by a Japanese government minister on interest rates, indirectly capped the dollar/yen's rise, but the currency market mostly shrugged off his commments.
Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Taro Aso was quoted as saying in an interview with Dow Jones in New York on Sunday that a rise in the official discount rate is "very possible" by the end of this year.
A long-term credit bank dealer said: "The market has been led by day-traders in Tokyo today, with many investors were unwilling to build fresh positions."
Dealers said Japanese institutional investors were still willing to buy dollars on dips, while Japanese exporters were lining up offers above 119 yen.
The upper side of the dollar was also capped by offers by U.S. fund operators and possible selling interest by a Chinese bank below 119 yen on Monday, dealers said.
Longer term, the dollar may test 120 yen amid healthier market fundamentals in the United States than Japan, which has kept the interest rate gap between the two nations wide.
"120 yen has come in sight. A clear break above 119.20 yen should send the dollar to 120 yen," Sakura's Nihei said.

The dollar maintained its bullish tone against the mark through the day after surging in New York on Friday due to fresh evidence of strength in the U.S. economy, such as stronger-than-expected U.S. non-farm payrolls data and the National Association of Purchasing Management data, which fuelled expectations of higher interest rates.
The dollar ended at 118.35/45 yen and 1.8620/30 marks after rising as high as 1.8665 marks in New York on Friday.
The mark stood near 63.45/48 yen by late Tokyo, compared with 63.67 yen in early trade.
